column3: Directly links denial of al-akhirah to present deviation from the path.
Opens the passage with a sign disclosed to the servant, supplying its revelatory setting.
Adds delayed repentance at death to the prepared painful consequence.
Shows how denial of al-akhirah makes deeds appear attractive and produces bewilderment.
Supplies the passage's earlier guidance and exclusive reliance frame.
Sets belief and turning away before the consequence of blazing fire.
Shows denial of al-akhirah constraining judgment of an unseen order.
Contributes the nearby exemplar of a grateful servant, without developing the warning.
Contrasts shared pain with hope expected from Allah.
Pairs refusal of belief with a consequence already prepared for deniers.
Provides the immediately preceding promise of great reward to believing doers.
Adds individual responsibility, a secondary judgment principle.
Shows hearts of those denying al-akhirah inclining, approving, and acquiring wrongdoing.
Begins the passage's announced pattern of corruption and consequence.
Frames painful punishment as the subject of protective prophetic warning.
Names deniers of al-akhirah as already in punishment and far error.
Provides a nearby fulfilled promise, supporting the passage's consequence pattern.
Characterizes deficient belief as rejection of the delivered message.
Specifies prepared restraints and blaze for the deniers.
Contributes the nearby historical reversal, not the final warning itself.
Uses ready material in a judgment scene, clarifying the preparation motif.
Joins denial and historical sign to a prepared painful punishment for wrongdoers.
Connects conduct to its own return and introduces a latter promise in the passage.
Uses otherness only as a local designation, without bearing on 17:10.
Relates prohibited exploitation to a prepared painful punishment for deniers.
Immediately continues the passage with mercy, recurrence, and hell for deniers.
Uses the safety sense of the root, not the belief-and-consequence reading.
Confirms that a prepared hell follows taking protectors apart from Allah.
Immediately follows with human haste, contrasting human urgency with divine preparation.
Uses the same painful-punishment formula against hypocritical appearance.
Extends painful consequence across the present life and al-akhirah, while retaining return as a possibility.
Adds signs, numbered years, and accounting to the passage's ordered temporal frame.
Affirms Allah's possession of both al-akhirah and the first life.
Places belief or denial before a fire explicitly described as prepared.
Presses the question of what further discourse could elicit belief after this message.
Sets faithful righteous action and increased bounty against arrogant refusal and painful punishment.
Directly links denial of the Hour to a blaze already prepared.
Contrasts Allah's guardianship of believers with deniers having no guardian.
Treats selective disbelief as real denial and joins it to prepared degrading punishment.
States the certain coming of the Hour and resurrection from graves.
Qualifies presumptions of safety from the Lord's punishment.
Supplies a warning against exalting oneself over Allah, with little direct overlap.
Supplies the positive horizon: belief in Allah and the Last Day with good action, without fear or grief.
Adds that the reward of believers is not lost.
Extends consequence across earlier and later generations.
States the endpoint is to the Lord, supporting the final-account horizon.
Shows spoken acts retained by an ever-ready watcher, giving a mechanism of readiness.
Links refusal of Allah's signs to lack of guidance and painful punishment.
Grounds the other arising in divine responsibility, supporting resurrection.
Joins hostile striving against signs to painful punishment.
Distinguishes a pressure-born claim of belief from enduring response.
Links disbelief, rejection of signs, and denial of meeting al-akhirah to being brought into punishment.
Uses laterness for a later group, not the final destination.
Places questioning truthfulness beside prepared painful punishment for deniers.
Shows believers enduring harm, only indirectly related to the warning.
Restates a prepared painful punishment for wrongdoers.
Keeps forgiveness and painful requital together in a repeated prophetic warning.
Indicates an additional punishment for wrongdoers beyond an unstated one.
Uses laterness for a group count, without illuminating 17:10.
Places alienation and prepared degrading punishment in both present life and al-akhirah.
Completes 27:4: those whose deeds are beautified receive the worst punishment and final loss.
Links denial of al-akhirah to denying hearts and arrogance.
Offers creation as a sign for believers, with only indirect relevance.
Within the same surah, shows a concealed barrier between Quran recitation and deniers of al-akhirah.
Relates faith to equitable social conduct, only secondarily to 17:10.
Associates denial of al-akhirah with the evil likeness, contrasting Allah's highest likeness.
Qualifies belief by showing it can remain internally divided through association.
Shows emotional aversion to Allah's sole mention among deniers of al-akhirah.
Uses preparation for a social scene, not the judgmental preparation of 17:10.
Extends punishment of deniers through this life and al-akhirah, without helpers.
Adds a before-and-after accounting frame, but not the focus's belief condition.
Places deniers of al-akhirah among those following desire and equating others with their Lord.
Offers changing provision as a sign for believers, only indirectly related.
Makes nonbelief the explicit question after cumulative signs.
Provides the positive counterpart: believers are certain of al-akhirah.
Shows belief withheld until painful punishment becomes visible, sharpening the warning's temporal force.
Uses laterness for enduring remembrance, not the final consequence.
Links trading away Allah's covenant to deprivation in al-akhirah and painful punishment.
Uses the others for a historical opposing group, without relevance to al-akhirah.
Mentions painful punishment for deniers but adds no specific connection.
Uses trustworthiness in a transmission description, not the focus's belief reading.
Places painful punishment for moral harm in this life and al-akhirah.
Uses laterness for enduring remembrance, not the final consequence.
Names a people disbelieving in Allah and al-akhirah, contrasted with divinely taught understanding.
Uses laterness for shared remembrance, without relevance to 17:10.
Links exchanging belief for disbelief to painful punishment.
Contrasts believing righteous response and added bounty with severe punishment for deniers.
Joins al-akhirah, mercy, punishment, and belief in signs within a conditional response frame.
Uses laterness for enduring remembrance, not the final consequence.
Mentions punishment of deniers within a contingent conflict setting.
Uses the others for a historical opposing group, without relevance to al-akhirah.
Frames nonbelief as refusal to turn the messenger's speech into believing reception.
Contrasts believers' increased faith and deniers' question in a fire-related test.
Shows that even complete delivery does not mechanically yield belief.
Links partial belief and partial denial to shame now and severe punishment at resurrection.
Provides the positive contrast that reminder benefits believers.
Anchors worship in creation and return to the Creator.
Shows belief as renewed, active response with mercy, light, and forgiveness.
Connects belief to steadfastness and remembrance, only indirectly.
Places false worship before an unavoidable account with the Lord and failed denial.
Within the same passage, contrasts pursuit of the immediate with an ensuing hell.
Within the same passage, supplies the positive counterpart: intending al-akhirah, striving, and belief.
Directly supplies a fire described as prepared for deniers.
Reiterates the fire prepared for deniers in an imperative warning.
Uses the prepared-punishment formula for deniers, with humiliation as its stated quality.
Repeats the prepared humiliating punishment for deniers in a conflict context.
Links divine rejection of deniers to a blaze prepared for them.
Links lack of expectation of meeting Allah to contentment with the immediate life and heedlessness of signs.
Gives fire as the destination of the preceding orientation toward the immediate life.
Explicitly identifies preferring the immediate life over al-akhirah as the ground of disbelief and lost guidance.
Begins the contrast in which transgression and preference for the immediate life lead to the fire.
Begins the contrary reading: fear of standing before the Lord and restraint from desire lead to the garden.
Explicitly names preference for the immediate life.
States that al-akhirah is better and more enduring.
Introduces a blazing fire as warning.
Identifies the one who denies and turns away as the one encountering that fire.
Gives the fire as the abode of the preceding preference for the immediate life.
Gives the garden as the abode of the contrary posture of restraint before the Lord.
States that only the most wretched enters the warned blazing fire.
